title: The Harmony of Instruction — The Church and Its Mission
content:
The Church and Its Mission

Read Instructions · Instructions index · Beyond the Torah · Counting and classification guide

This Harmony follows themes through Christ, the apostles, parables, wisdom and the prophets. Open the complementary Christ-study collection. The two views serve different purposes; their entry counts are not added together.

The Harmony of Instruction · His own commandments: until He comes · Christ, the apostles, the parables, Proverbs and the Psalms

← Treasure, Trust and Watchfulness · The Harmony of Instruction: all subjects

What He gave His disciples to do together and to carry to the nations: the Supper, baptism and teaching, the sending, the shepherding of His flock.

Each section follows one order: the word of Christ; the apostles who hand it on; the parables; the wisdom of Proverbs; the Psalms; and the Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture. Verses of Proverbs and the Psalms are quoted in full from the Saints Translation; everything else is linked to the place where it is given in full. Psalms are numbered as in the Greek, with the Hebrew number in parentheses. The selection is an editor’s gathering: a doorway into the text, not an addition to it.

On this page: Do This in Remembrance of Me · Go and Make Disciples · The Sending · Shepherds of the Flock

Do This in Remembrance of Me

Do this in remembrance of Me. Behind the Supper stand the Passover kept as a memorial, the blood of the covenant sprinkled at Sinai, the bread from heaven, Melchizedek’s loaves and wine, and Wisdom, who mixed her wine, prepared her table and sent out her servants to call.

The word of Christ

91. To take and eat: this is His body; to drink of the cup: this is His blood of the covenant; to do this in remembrance of Him. Luke 22:19–20

And He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body [which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.” And likewise the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, poured out for you.]

Luke 22:19–20

92. Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in yourselves. John 6:53–56

The apostles hand it on

7. To keep the Supper as received from the Lord: this is My body, this cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this in remembrance of Me. 1 Corinthians 11:23–26

For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread, and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.” Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.” For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

1 Corinthians 11:23–26

100. Christ our Passover has been sacrificed; let us keep the feast with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. 1 Corinthians 5:6–8

101. A priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek. Hebrews 7:1–3 · Hebrews 7:15–17

In parable

The Great Supper. Those first invited made excuses; the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame are brought in.

The Wedding Feast. Many are called, but few are chosen.

The wisdom of Proverbs

Wisdom built herself a house,
and set seven pillars beneath it.
She slaughtered her own sacrificial animals,
mixed her own wine in a mixing-bowl,
and prepared her own table.
She sent her own servants,
summoning with a lofty proclamation to the mixing-bowl, saying:
“Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me!”
And to those lacking understanding she said:
“Come, eat of my loaves,
and drink wine that I mixed for you.
Leave foolishness, and you will live;
seek understanding, so that you may live,
and set insight right in knowledge.”

Proverbs 9:1–6

In the Psalms

You prepared a table before me opposite those who afflict me;
You enriched my head with oil,
and Your cup is intoxicating—how excellent!

Psalm 22 (23):5

What shall I repay to the Lord
for everything He has repaid to me?
I will take the cup of salvation
and call on the name of the Lord.

Psalm 115 (116):3–4

Taste and see that the Lord is kind;
blessed is the man who hopes in Him.

Psalm 33 (34):9

and rained manna for them to eat,
and gave them heaven’s bread.
A human ate angels’ bread;
He sent them food supplies to fullness.

Psalm 77 (78):24–25

He made remembrance of His wonders;
the Lord is merciful and compassionate.
He gave food to those who fear Him;
He will remember His covenant forever.

Psalm 110 (111):4–5

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

In the commandments of the Law: 408. To eat the Passover with unleavened bread and bitter herbs

Melchizedek brings out loaves and wine Genesis 14:18
A memorial for you Exodus 12:14
The bread the Lord has given Exodus 16:15
The blood of the covenant Exodus 24:8
The life of the flesh is its blood Leviticus 17:11
Come, buy without silver Isaiah 55:1–3
The new covenant Jeremiah 38:31–34
By covenant blood Zechariah 9:11
A pure sacrifice among the nations Malachi 1:11

Go and Make Disciples

All authority has been given to Me: Daniel saw it given to one like a son of man. Go to all the nations: the promise to Abram, the light of Isaiah, the song of the Psalms. And He breathed on them, as God breathed into the first man a breath of life.

The word of Christ

93. To go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to observe everything He commanded. Matthew 28:18–20

Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and upon earth has been given to Me. Go, therefore, and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe everything I commanded you. And behold, I am with you all the days until the consummation of the age.”

Matthew 28:18–20

94. That repentance and forgiveness of sins be proclaimed in His name to all the nations; to remain in the city until clothed with power from on high. Luke 24:46–49

95. As the Father has sent Me, I also send you. Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive are forgiven. John 20:21–23

The apostles hand it on

1. To repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and to receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. Acts 2:38–39

Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each one of you be baptized upon the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you, for your children, and for all who are far away—as many as the Lord our God calls to Himself.”

Acts 2:38–39

2. To bear witness to Him to the end of the earth; He commanded us to proclaim that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name. Acts 10:42–43

6. To be buried with Him through baptism into death, and to walk in newness of life. Romans 6:3–4

42. Is anyone among you sick? Let him call the elders of the church to pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord; confess your sins to one another. James 5:14–16

80. Scripture foresaw that God would justify the nations by faith: In you all the nations will be blessed. Galatians 3:8–9

110. This is what was spoken through the prophet Joel: I will pour out My Spirit upon all flesh. Acts 2:16–21

112. You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for His possession. 1 Peter 2:9–10

In parable

The Mustard Seed. The smallest of seeds becomes a tree in whose branches the birds make their dwelling.

The Leaven. A little leaven hidden in three measures of flour leavens the whole.

The Dragnet. The net gathers every kind; at the end of the age the angels separate the evil from the righteous.

The Sower. The seed is the word; the four soils are four ways of hearing it. The Lord explains it Himself.

The Seed Growing of Itself. The kingdom grows as seed does, night and day, the sower knows not how, until the harvest.

The wisdom of Proverbs

From the fruit of righteousness a tree of life grows,
but the lives of lawless people are taken away before their time.

Proverbs 11:30

A faithful witness will rescue a life from evils,
but a deceitful person kindles lies.

Proverbs 14:25

Rescue those being led to death,
and ransom those being killed; do not hold back.

Proverbs 24:11

As cold water is welcome to a thirsty life,
so is good news from a faraway land.

Proverbs 25:25

In the Psalms

Sing to the Lord; bless His name.
Proclaim the good news of His salvation day after day.
Announce His glory among the nations,
His wonders among all the peoples.

Psalm 95 (96):2–3

Their sound went out into all the earth,
and their utterances to the limits of the inhabited world.
In the sun He set His dwelling.

Psalm 18 (19):5

All the limits of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord,
and all the families of the nations will bow down before You,
because kingship belongs to the Lord,
and He is master of the nations.

Psalm 21 (22):28–29

Praise the Lord, all nations;
laud Him, all peoples,

Psalm 116 (117):1

That Your way may be known on earth,
Your salvation among all nations.

Psalm 66 (67):3

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

The breath of life Genesis 2:7
All the tribes of the earth blessed Genesis 12:3
All the nations will come Isaiah 2:2–3
Here I am: send me Isaiah 6:8
A light for nations Isaiah 49:6
The feet of one bringing good news Isaiah 52:7
Good news to the poor Isaiah 61:1
Authority given to one like a son of man Daniel 7:13–14
My Spirit upon all flesh Joel 3:1
The earth filled with knowing the Lord’s glory Habakkuk 2:14
Ten men from all the nations Zechariah 8:23

The Sending

He sends them as the prophets were sent: with words put in the mouth, without inheritance, in haste like Gehazi, to be mocked as the messengers were mocked. Those who sow in tears will reap with exultation.

The word of Christ

96. To proclaim that the kingdom has drawn near, to heal the sick; freely you received, freely give. Matthew 10:7–8

As you go, proclaim, ‘The kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.’ Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give.

Matthew 10:7–8

97. To take nothing for the road, to remain in one house, and to shake off the dust where you are not received. Mark 6:8–11

98. When they hand you over, not to be anxious how or what you will speak. Matthew 10:19–20

99. When they persecute you in one city, to flee to the next. Matthew 10:23

100. To rejoice and be glad when you are reviled and persecuted for His sake. Matthew 5:11–12

Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say every evil thing against you because of Me. Rejoice and exult, for your reward is great in the heavens; for in this way they persecuted the prophets before you.

Matthew 5:11–12

101. Not to rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but that your names are written in the heavens. Luke 10:20

102. Not to stop the one who does a mighty work in His name: whoever is not against us is for us. Mark 9:39–40

The apostles hand it on

8. To remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive. Acts 20:35

In everything I showed you that by working in this way we must support the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

Acts 20:35

30. To receive and send on their way the brothers who went out for the sake of the Name, and so to become fellow workers for the truth. 3 John 1:5–8

47. The Lord directed that those who proclaim the good news should live from the good news; the worker is worthy of his wages. 1 Corinthians 9:14

54. To rejoice insofar as you share Christ’s sufferings; if you are reviled for the name of Christ, you are blessed. 1 Peter 4:12–14

55. To count it all joy when you fall into various trials, for the testing of your faith produces endurance. James 1:2–4

76. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and have seen the Lord’s purpose. James 5:10–11

83. You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes: it was written for our sake, that the worker should share the crop. 1 Corinthians 9:8–11

115. Whom the Lord loves He disciplines; endure it as sons. Hebrews 12:5–11

In parable

The Sower. The seed is the word; the four soils are four ways of hearing it. The Lord explains it Himself.

The Workers in the Vineyard. The last receive as the first, for the master is generous; the last will be first and the first last.

The Grain of Wheat. Unless it falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.

The Woman in Labor. Her grief turns to joy when the child is born: so your grief will become joy.

The wisdom of Proverbs

An impious person flees when no one pursues,
but a righteous person is confident like a lion.

Proverbs 28:1

Son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline or lose heart when corrected by Him,
for the Lord disciplines the one He loves and scourges every son He receives.

Proverbs 3:11–12

As silver and gold are tested in a furnace,
so hearts are chosen before the Lord.

Proverbs 17:3

In the Psalms

Those sowing in tears
will reap with exultation.
Going, they went and wept,
carrying their seeds;
but coming, they will arrive with exultation,
carrying their sheaves.

Psalm 125 (126):5–6

For Your sake we are put to death all day long;
we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.

Psalm 43 (44):23

for on Your account I endured reproach;
embarrassment covered my face.

Psalm 68 (69):8

Many are the afflictions of the righteous,
and He will rescue them from them all.

Psalm 33 (34):20

The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup;
You are the One who restores my inheritance to me.

Psalm 15 (16):5

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

I will open your mouth Exodus 4:10–12
Blot me out of the book Exodus 32:32
Eldad and Medad Numbers 11:26–29
I am your share and your inheritance Numbers 18:20
Greet no one on the road 2 Kings 4:29
They mocked His prophets 2 Chronicles 36:15–16
Shaken out Nehemiah 5:13
Hated for the Name Isaiah 66:5
I have put My words in your mouth Jeremiah 1:7–9
A fire in my bones Jeremiah 20:9
Do not fear them Ezekiel 2:6–7
The Lord took me from the sheep Amos 7:14–15

Shepherds of the Flock

Feed My lambs. The charge to Peter answers Moses’ prayer that the congregation not be like sheep without a shepherd, and the long complaint of the prophets against shepherds who fed themselves. Proverbs gives the pastor’s rule in a line: know thoroughly the lives of your flock.

The word of Christ

103. To feed His lambs and shepherd His sheep. John 21:15–17

So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus says to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, You know that I love You.” He says to him, “Feed My lambs.” He says to him again a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, You know that I love You.” He says to him, “Shepherd My sheep.” He says to him the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was grieved because He said to him the third time, “Do you love Me?” And he said to Him, “Lord, You know all things; You know that I love You.” Jesus says to him, “Feed My sheep.

John 21:15–17

104. When you have turned back, to strengthen your brothers. Luke 22:32

105. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven. Matthew 18:18

The apostles hand it on

26. Elders are to shepherd the flock of God willingly, not lording it over those in their charge but being examples. 1 Peter 5:1–4

Therefore, I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a participant in the glory about to be revealed: Shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion but willingly, according to God; not for shameful gain but eagerly; not as lording it over those allotted to you, but becoming examples to the flock. And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.

1 Peter 5:1–4

In parable

The Good Shepherd and the Door. The sheep hear His voice; the good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep. John calls it a figure of speech.

The Lost Sheep. There is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.

The Shepherds and the Sheep. Woe to the shepherds who feed themselves; the Lord Himself will seek His sheep. The Lord’s word, I am the good Shepherd, answers this prophecy.

The Faithful and the Wicked Slave. Blessed is the slave whom his master finds so doing when he comes.

The wisdom of Proverbs

Know thoroughly the lives of your flock,
and set your heart upon your herds;

Proverbs 27:23

Mercy and truth are a guard for a king,
and they will surround his throne in righteousness.

Proverbs 20:28

In the Psalms

And He chose David His servant,
and took him up from the flocks of sheep;
from behind the ewes giving birth He took him,
to shepherd Jacob His people
and Israel His inheritance.
And he shepherded them in his heart’s innocence,
and guided them with his hands’ understanding.

Psalm 77 (78):70–72

You who shepherd Israel, pay attention,
You who guide Joseph like sheep;
You who sit upon the cherubim, appear.

Psalm 79 (80):2

Restore to me the exultation of Your salvation,
and strengthen me with a governing spirit.
I will teach the lawless Your ways,
and the ungodly will turn back to You.

Psalm 50 (51):14–15

Know that the Lord—He is God.
He made us, and not we;
His people and the sheep of His pasture.

Psalm 99 (100):3

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

Sheep without a shepherd Numbers 27:16–17
You will shepherd My people 2 Samuel 5:2
He will tend His flock Isaiah 40:11
Shepherds according to My heart Jeremiah 3:15
Woe to the shepherds who scatter Jeremiah 23:1–4
Shepherds who feed themselves Ezekiel 34:2–4
I will seek out My sheep Ezekiel 34:11–16
One shepherd Ezekiel 34:23
He will shepherd in the Lord’s strength Micah 5:3
You who have abandoned the sheep Zechariah 11:17
